newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks ease in early see-saw trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks ease in early see-saw trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were easier on Thursday morning in see-saw trading as investors took profits after Wednesday's price rebound, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index lost 123 points, or 0.75 percent, to 16,359 after moving between 16,496.24 and 16,354.67. Turnover was at HK$9.42 billion.
"Blue chips are under light selling pressure but there is no special story to move the market decisively in either way," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Cheung Kong eased HK$0.25 to HK$92.75 and Henderson Land fell HK$1.00 to HK$72.00.

Sentiment on properties remained weak on worries that higher mortgage rates could dampen home buying interest, brokers said. A number of local banks have announced they would increase mortgage rates by 25 basis points to 9.25 percent.
It would be healthier for the market to consolidate before embarking on another rally, said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.

Light profit-taking alternated with bargain-hunting on China related stocks. The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporation Index for red chips rose 18 points to 3,878 but the H-share index lost 26 points, or 1.74 percent, to 1,502 at mid-morning.
